text:
South Korean stocks traded sharply higher late Friday morning, extending a tentative recovery after a volatile week, led by gains in technology shares amid continued market jitters over artificial intelligence (AI).
After opening 0.37 percent higher, the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) extended its earlier gains to trade up 105.42 points, or 2.24 percent, to 4,816.63 as of 11:20 a.m.
Investors are watching whether the tech rally has staying power after days of volatility driven by doubts over the sustainability of the AI trade.
Overnight, Wall Street was closed for the Thanksgiving holiday.
In Seoul, large-cap shares were trading higher across the board.
Market bellwether Samsung Electronics went up 1.98 percent and its chipmaking rival SK hynix gained 1.71 percent after both opened lower.
Among other index heavyweights, SK Square, the parent of SK hynix, added 1.84 percent, while battery maker LG Energy Solution gained 3.15 percent.
The Korean won was quoted at 1,341.3 won against the U.S. dollar as of 11:20 a.m., up 2.6 won from the previous stock trading session's close.
